args: set -euo pipefail; n=$(cargo test -q -p tier-drop-core -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': test$'); echo "tests: $n"; test "$n" -ge 25

set -euo pipefail; for f in registry qos plan floors disqualify decide holdout eval dataset review; do n=$(cargo test -q -p tier-drop-core "$f" -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': test$' || true); test "$n" -ge 1 || { echo "no test selected by $f"; exit 1; }; done

evidence_required: Output of cargo test -p tier-drop-core with the test count.
Output of cargo clippy -p tier-drop-core --all-targets -- -D warnings.
objective: Implement the pure tier-drop-core library: the data contracts as typed records and every engine function with the exact signatures, the registry example and default policy, and per-requirement tests, building for wasm32.

outputs.purpose: Rust modules tier, registry, task, candidate, attempt, disqualification, decision, plan, eval, policy, canonical, rights and their unit tests.
Core manifest (deps: serde, serde_json, sha2, schemars, hex or manual hex).
Indicative example registry as of 2026-10-19 with deployment ids only.
Default policy embedded in the core.
Workspace lockfile updated for the core dependencies.

risk_controls: The library has no std::fs, std::time, rand or network use; all ids and timestamps are parameters.
Rust by default; strict TypeScript only in adapters/dsh; no Python and no authored .js, .mjs or .cjs files.
No secret, phone number, account identifier or internal hostname in any file; run gitleaks protect --staged --redact before each commit.
Never write the owner's private organisation name (search pattern O[K]OA) or the forbidden owner-framing phrase (search pattern needs[ ]you) into any file; plain, specific prose.
Work only in the slice's worktree and branch; never touch main.
steps: Implement the types of plan/technology-decisions.md "Data contracts" in crates/core/src/ as modules: tier, registry, task, candidate, attempt, disqualification, decision, plan, eval, policy, canonical (canonical JSON + record_sha256), rights. #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], schemars::JsonSchema derives on every record type.

Implement functions with exactly these signatures (module paths free): validate_registry(&Registry) -> Vec<Issue> (Issue { code: String, message: String }); validate_task(&Task, &Policy) -> Vec<Issue> (floors cover required_floors; strict-review rule R-22); qos_gate(&Registry, &Task, &Policy) -> QosGateResult; ladder(&Task, &Registry, &Policy) -> Vec<Tier>; plan_next(&Task, &Registry, &[Disqualification], &[Attempt], &Policy) -> Plan; check_floors(&Task, &Attempt, &Policy) -> FloorResult; assess_disqualification(family: &str, tier: Tier, &[Attempt], &Task, registry_as_of: &str, &Policy) -> Option<Disqualification>; decide(&Task, &Registry, &[Disqualification], &[Attempt], &Policy) -> RoutingDecision; split_holdout(&[EvalItem], &Policy) -> EvalSplit; summarise_eval taking (family, tier, &Candidate, &[Attempt], &[Floor]) and returning EvalRun; dataset_filter<'a>(&'a [Attempt], Purpose) -> Vec<&'a Attempt> (Purpose::{Process, Train, SendRemote, Export}); canonical_json(&serde_json::Value) -> String, record_sha256(&serde_json::Value) -> String (excludes the record_sha256 key); schemas() -> BTreeMap<&'static str, schemars::Schema> for the names listed under the CLI schemas command; Policy::default() equals registry/policy.default.json; Registry::example() parses registry/registry.example.json (both via include_str!).

Write registry/registry.example.json: the commission's indicative models as of 2026-10-19 across tiers 1–4 (Jev, Laya; a Docling model, a Qwen OCR model, a ScaleDown model; DeepSeek 4.1 Flash, Qwen 3.8 27B, GLM-5.3-flash; GLM-5.3, Qwen 3.8 Max, Mistral 4, Kimi K3, Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1-Sol), one tailored example bound to a family, two embedding helpers, deployments with ids only (local-mbp, local-mini, zai, anthropic, openai, deepseek), plausible placeholder costs and QoS marked as example values in notes. No hostnames, no keys.

Unit tests per requirement, named so cargo test -p tier-drop-core registry|qos|plan|floors|disqualify|decide|holdout|eval|dataset|review each select at least one test. Property-style tests for split_holdout determinism and whole-family assignment.
cargo fmt, cargo clippy -p tier-drop-core --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test -p tier-drop-core.
